source_title: Why markets rallied: Sensex jumps over 900 points, Nifty gains 1 per cent; 5 key reasons
source_excerpt: Indian stock markets rallied sharply on Thursday, with the Sensex rising over 900 points to close at 74,151 and the Nifty gaining more than 1% to settle at 22,936.75. The gains came on the monthly derivatives expiry day, supported by a firmer rupee, a marginal easing in crude oil prices, the US Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged, and strong corporate earnings. Buying also spread to mid-cap and small-cap stocks, signalling improved investor sentiment after a recent period of consolidation.The Nifty crossed its key 20-day exponential moving average (20-DEMA) level of around 22,825 during the session. It extended its gains through the afternoon as buying picked up across sectors. Realty, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) and select banking stocks led the advance.Here are five key factors behind Thursday's market rally.Rupee begins the day on a stronger noteThe rupee opened higher against the US dollar, supporting sentiment in domestic equities. A stronger rupee can help ease the cost of imports, particularly crude oil, which India relies heavily on. Currency movements also influence foreign investors' returns and can affect their appetite for Indian stocks.Crude oil prices ease marginallyBrent crude prices eased slightly but remained elevated at around $114-$115 per barrel. The modest decline offered some relief to oil-importing India, where high crude prices can increase import costs, put pressure on the rupee and fuel inflation.However, concerns over possible supply disruptions in West Asia continued to pose a risk. Sustained relief from high energy costs will depend on whether oil prices decline further.US Federal Reserve holds interest rates steadyThe US Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75%-4%, easing concerns about an immediate increase in borrowing costs. The decision supported risk appetite, although persistent inflation concerns remain.The outlook for US interest rates matters for Indian markets because it influences global bond yields, the dollar's strength and foreign fund flows into emerging markets such as India.Strong corporate earnings support buyingPositive corporate earnings helped support buying in select stocks, particularly in realty, FMCG and banking. The gains reflected investor interest in companies with resilient business performance.Analysts, however, said the recovery needs sustained buying across sectors to establish a more durable upward trend.Mid-cap and small-cap stocks join the rallyThe rally extended beyond the benchmark indices, with mid-cap and small-cap stocks also recording solid gains. The broader participation suggested that buying interest had improved following a brief phase of consolidation.Ajit Mishra, senior vice-president of research at Religare Broking, said the recovery reflected improved risk appetite and renewed buying interest."Markets staged a strong rebound on Thursday, gaining over 1% amid favourable cues and improved investor sentiment. After opening on a flat note, the Nifty crossed the key hurdle around 20 DEMA and gradually moved higher to settle at 22,936.75. The Sensex advanced over 900 points to close at 74,151 on the expiry day, reflecting improved risk appetite and renewed buying interest," Mishra said.He added that the breadth of the rally was encouraging, but further gains would require sustained buying across sectors."On the sectoral front, buying was visible across several pockets, with realty, FMCG and select banking stocks leading the recovery. The broad-based advance indicates an improvement in market participation following the recent correction. However, sustained buying across sectors will be essential to establish a more durable recovery."Among the key macro factors, the US Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate at 3.75%â4%, while its commentary highlighted persistent inflation concerns. Global bond yields, dollar movements and expectations surrounding the future interest-rate trajectory will therefore remain in focus.
